title: Jam sessions with George Foster and Deep Forest
summary: Albert recalls a Chicago jam session where George Foster and others played Deep Forest with no horns, and how he came upon it.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Testing. January 1st, 1974. We're on the second side of this first reel of Don Alba. We're talking about how Earl Hines was a big thing in Chicago coming on with Deep Forest.

And George Foster would be on the piano and you could hear those knockers, click and click, click click click click click. And this guy blowing like Lil Armstrong. No horn, just making lifts. And this guy playing the bass, boom boom boom. And we'd stand, George Foster would cock his head on the side and say, you all hit? And one of the guys said, yes father, we hit. Keep going man. And they would play the whole tune of Deep Forest with no music coming out at all. And I'd be standing up there laughing, just dying laughing at what

Well, who would stand up there? You? Well, I would possibly go down there to see him about fixing the horn and straightening the mule out of something like that. And I would happen upon this jam session.
